title: Brightline Rail — telemetry into a Fabric lakehouse

tabs.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Brightline Rail operates freight services across four regions. Every locomotive emits telemetry — position, fuel, temperature and fault codes — and the engineering team wants that data available for both live monitoring and historical analysis.
A data engineering team of four has built the first version in Microsoft Fabric. It works, but it was built quickly and several decisions are now being revisited.

tabs.heading: Existing environment
paragraphs: One F64 capacity backs three workspaces: BL-Dev, BL-Test and BL-Prod, joined by a deployment pipeline. BL-Dev is connected to Git.

Locomotive telemetry arrives continuously as events, roughly 4,000 per second at peak. A separate nightly extract of maintenance records arrives as CSV files in an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 account owned by the maintenance system vendor.

A lakehouse named lh_telemetry holds bronze and silver Delta tables. A warehouse named wh_reporting holds the gold layer, which the finance and operations teams query with T-SQL, including a nightly procedure that writes reconciliation rows.
A notebook rewrites the entire silver table on every run. It now takes 50 minutes and the silver table has grown to several thousand small Parquet files.
Engineers currently need Workspace Contributor in BL-Prod to read pipeline run history, which the platform lead considers too broad.

tabs.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: Locomotive events must be queryable within seconds of arriving, for a live operations dashboard.
The vendor's CSV files must be readable from lh_telemetry without being copied, because the vendor's account remains the system of record.
Query performance against the silver table must improve without changing the notebook's transformation logic.
Finance and operations must keep running their existing T-SQL, including the nightly procedure that writes rows.
Engineers must be able to read pipeline run history in BL-Prod without gaining the ability to change items there.
Nothing may be edited directly in BL-Prod; every change reaches production through the deployment pipeline.
